channel.title: Sophie's Morning Brief
channel.description: A daily 30-minute news briefing made just for Sophie.
channel.itunes:author: Claude

item.title: 10.31.26 · Kingmakers in black hats, a $6.3B heist, DoorDash's big buy
item.description: Israel's coalition maze gets stranger as an ultra-Orthodox faction reportedly weighs talking to the opposition and Yair Golan rejects a unity government; North Korean hackers are blamed for stealing 6.3 billion dollars from Binance in the biggest crypto heist ever; DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for 17 billion dollars.

item.title: 10.30.26 · The final count, a foreign-money probe, Kalshi's $40B day
item.description: Israel finishes counting with Likud at 27 seats and the deadlock unchanged as the elections chief asks the Shin Bet to probe suspected foreign funding; Iran says four tankers hit mines in Hormuz as the US tells allies to prepare for strikes after the midterms; Kalshi hits a 40 billion dollar valuation the same week Utah files criminal charges.

item.title: 10.29.26 · The soldiers' vote, a "stolen" claim, Bolsonaro in Miami
item.description: Israel counts the last half million soldiers' and absentee ballots with Netanyahu's bloc stuck at 53 seats as Likud claims Arab parties "stole" the election; Trump says a strike on Iran after the midterms is "possible" as Tehran weighs a Qatari peace draft; Brazil's defeated Flávio Bolsonaro flees to Miami.

item.title: 10.28.26 · Likud comes first, nobody wins, Jay-Z gets the Super Bowl
item.description: Likud finishes as Israel's largest party but neither bloc reaches 61 seats as a long count begins; Netanyahu calls Iran a "historic, one-time opportunity" as the US reportedly warns Gulf states of a short war after the midterms; Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl halftime show.

item.title: 10.27.26 · Israel votes, an Iran strike on hold, Intel's quantum deal
item.description: Israel votes today after reports that Netanyahu pushed Trump for a pre-election strike on Iran and was told to wait; Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials hold first-ever joint talks in Tehran; Intel buys Israeli quantum startup Classiq for two point three billion dollars.

item.title: 10.26.26 · Lula's comeback, a clash over Iran, Israel votes tomorrow
item.description: Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil as Flávio Bolsonaro refuses to concede; Israel's army chief reportedly resists a Netanyahu order on Iran a day before the election; Serbia's Vučić concedes defeat to a student-led movement.

item.title: 10.25.26 · Trump's "maybe tomorrow", a huge rally, Brazil decides
item.description: Trump says a strike on Iran could come "maybe tomorrow" as an Iranian lawmaker raises nuclear weapons; tens of thousands rally in Tel Aviv for an October seventh inquiry two days before Israel votes; Brazil chooses between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro today with the final polls at fifty-one to forty-nine.

item.title: 10.24.26 · Hebron attack, a strike "absolutely" possible, Brazil votes
item.description: Two Israeli soldiers are killed in a Hebron checkpoint attack and the city is sealed three days before Israel votes; a US envoy says a strike on Iran could "absolutely" come this weekend as Brent tops 117 dollars; Brazil picks between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a dead-heat runoff tomorrow.

item.title: 10.23.26 · Final polls, Hormuz flare-up, Art Basel shuts early
item.description: The last Israeli polls before the ban show a dead heat four days before the vote; Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims hits on seven ships as Brent tops 112 dollars; Art Basel Paris closes two days early as France braces for more protests.

item.title: 10.22.26 · Iran strike plans, Eisenkot's red line, Lander detained
item.description: The US and Israel reportedly plan new strikes on Iran after the US midterms as Netanyahu orders the regime's overthrow; Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu five days before the vote; New York's Brad Lander is detained by Israeli troops at a West Bank olive harvest.

item.title: 10.21.26 · Eisenkot widens lead, Iran says no, Sixers spoil ring night
item.description: New polls show Eisenkot's Yashar ahead with neither bloc near 61 seats six days before Israel's election; Iran tells mediators its enriched uranium will never leave the country as oil tops 111 dollars; the 76ers beat the Knicks on championship banner night.

item.title: 10.20.26 · Gantz bows out, Egypt waits, Shashua's $200M AI bet
item.description: Benny Gantz pulls out of Israel's election a week before the vote; Egypt's parliament delays its vote on defending Saudi Arabia as Russia's Lavrov lands in Tehran; Amnon Shashua's new startup doubleAI launches with two hundred million dollars.

item.title: 10.19.26 · Trump endorses Bibi, Egypt eyes war, Wiz buys McDonald's?
item.description: Trump gives Netanyahu his "complete and total endorsement" eight days before Israel's election; Egypt moves toward defending Saudi Arabia against the Houthis; Wiz's billionaire founders close in on buying McDonald's Israel.

item.title: 10.18.26 · Hormuz on fire, diplomats attacked, Varonis sells for $6.3B
item.description: Iran claims tankers hit mines in Hormuz as oil nears $110; settlers attack European diplomats in the West Bank and Rubio steps in; Israeli data-security pioneer Varonis is sold to Proofpoint for six point three billion dollars.

item.title: 10.15.26 · Escalation warnings, a Shin Bet lawsuit, a $42M Kandinsky
item.description: Israel's army chief warns of escalation before the election; ex-Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar sues Netanyahu over October 7 blame; Christie's London makes $289 million, led by a restituted Kandinsky.

item.title: 10.14.26 · Iran before the vote, Aramco hit, and the Pope's diagnosis
item.description: Netanyahu reportedly pressed Trump to resume the Iran war before Israel's election; the Houthis hit an Aramco building as the Saudi-Houthi war escalates; Pope Leo is diagnosed with lung cancer after surgery.

item.title: 10.13.26 · Airlines quit Riyadh, a hike turns deadly, Orion's $500M
item.description: Qatar Airways and Etihad suspend flights to Saudi cities as Houthi strikes continue; a teenager is killed by an old Hezbollah bomblet on a school hike in the north; CrowdStrike is in advanced talks to buy Israeli startup Orion for about five hundred million dollars.

item.title: 10.12.26 · Riyadh hit again, Bennett's phone line and a $7B Decart deal
item.description: Riyadh's airport is hit a fourth time as the FAA tells US airlines to use caution; Bennett tells Netanyahu he's "welcome to give me a call"; Amazon is in talks to buy Israeli-founded AI startup Decart for about seven billion dollars.

item.title: 10.11.26 · An American killed in Riyadh, and a race to the threshold
item.description: The Riyadh airport death toll climbs to twelve including an American as Trump weighs strikes; Gantz and Winter refuse to quit Israel's election race; Florence Pugh's East of Eden tops Netflix.

item.title: 10.10.26 · A Nobel snub, a Saint Laurent exit and a Gaza anniversary
item.description: Navi Pillay wins the Nobel Peace Prize and the US sanctions the ICC hours later; the UAE confirms the flydubai copilot planned a 9/11-style attack; Gaza's ceasefire turns one year old today.

item.title: 10.09.26 · Tampered records, a renamed consulate and a T. rex cousin
item.description: Netanyahu's former military secretary alleges October 7 records were altered; Britain's Jerusalem consulate is downgraded and twenty diplomats leave; Trump says no strike on Iran before the US midterms.

item.title: 10.08.26 · A tied race, a flydubai fallout and a Koons sale
item.description: A new poll shows Israel's election deadlocked; the flydubai scare puts Israelis' US visa waiver at risk; Mamdani's October 7 statement sparks a firestorm in New York.

item.title: 10.07.26 · Three years since October 7, and a race to the ballot box
item.description: Israel marks three years since October 7; Arab parties cleared for the October 27 election; a 450 million dollar Van Gogh and Cézanne sale heads to New York.
